answer: Forging a thousand sybils becomes a velvet trap: honest agents pay little, while attackers burn an umber tide of compute and forfeit stakes at the inlet of every epoch, making mass identity creation economically irrational. Each agent must stake a bonded deposit and solve a per-epoch proof-of-work whose difficulty rises with the number of identities claimed. In practice, Agent0144 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
